$comment: Tier 2 — your organisation's shared agent environment. This file is the authority for WHAT gets installed; install.sh is only the mechanism. It pins Tier 1 (the generic Dark Factory method) by COMMIT SHA and lists every shared skill and hook explicitly. When Tier 1 adds something, your org takes it by a deliberate edit here — never by surprise on the next install.

dark-factory.$refNote: A COMMIT SHA, resolved when this layer was generated. A branch name here means upstream can move under you between installs. Taking an update is a one-line bump — resolve the new SHA with: git ls-remote https://github.com/OneDro1d/dark-factory.git refs/heads/main

install.$comment: Filled by new-org-layer.sh from the Tier 1 checkout at generation time, then yours to curate. A DECLARATION is a name in the `skills`/`hooks` ARRAY; where it comes from is the matching entry in `skillSources`/`hookSources`. Sources: 'upstream:<vendored-repo>/<path>' resolves under vendor/; a bare '<vendored-repo>/<path>' means the same thing (the legacy form); 'local:<path>' resolves in THIS repo — that is where your org's own skills and hooks live (skills/, hooks/), and `local:` is resolved against THIS lockfile's directory, not against the installer's own location. A value containing '..' is refused, never normalised. A local entry with the same name as an upstream one overrides it; install.sh reports every override loudly, because a silent override is how tiers rot. This is the same shape lock-verify L7 checks, in both directions.

skillSources.$comment: skill-name -> source. Keys beginning with $ are documentation, not entries. Every name above must appear here and every entry here must be named above -- either half alone installs nothing while still reading like a declaration.

hookSources.$comment: hook-file-name -> source. Same both-directions rule as skillSources.

mcpNote: There is no single MCP tool prefix — the namespace depends on how each machine connects (account-level connector vs project-level .mcp.json hub), and two people in the same org can legitimately see different names in the same week. Treat any prefix written in docs as a data point to confirm, never a constant to copy. List the tools in YOUR session and check; if nothing resolves or it is ambiguous, ASK — a wrong prefix looks exactly like a missing tool, and an agent that wrongly concludes a system is unavailable may invent state rather than report the gap.

notRestorable.$comment: Printed by install.sh every run, so a green install is never mistaken for a complete setup.
notRestorable.gh auth login: credentials cannot live in a lockfile
notRestorable.MCP connectors: account- or project-level, authenticated interactively — confirm your tool namespace before relying on it
notRestorable.settings.json hook registration: yours to merge — the installer places files, it does not edit your settings
